Npgsql 5.0.18 Unity AOT compatibility build

View this file on GitHub

Pinned upstream source: https://github.com/npgsql/npgsql/tree/v5.0.18/src/Npgsql License: PostgreSQL (see LICENSE). Upstream signing identity and assembly/package version are retained so the existing EF Core PostgreSQL provider remains compatible.

Three upstream runtime methods are changed:

  • NpgsqlTypeHandler<TDefault>.GenerateNonGenericValidationMethod
  • NpgsqlSimpleTypeHandler<TDefault>.GenerateNonGenericValidationMethod
  • NpgsqlConnector.Connect: accept SocketError.InProgress as a pending non-blocking connection, alongside WouldBlock.

The two validator factories previously used Expression.Compile to create a delegate with a ref NpgsqlLengthCache argument. Unity's IL2CPP profile interprets expressions; its LightLambda.CreateCustomDelegate throws NotImplementedException("byref delegate"). This happens while opening the connection and initializing driver handlers, before any application SQL can run. Preserving more linker metadata cannot implement this missing interpreter operation.

The replacement uses an ordinary C# delegate, compiled ahead of time by IL2CPP, with an immutable dispatch table of the handler's implemented interfaces. Dispatch still matches the exact boxed CLR type, preserves null/DBNull handling in the original callers, copies a mutated ref length cache back even on exceptions, and unwraps TargetInvocationException with ExceptionDispatchInfo so caller-visible exception types and stacks are preserved. Simple validators leave the cache alone. No runtime compilation of a byref expression delegate is required. Both Mono and IL2CPP use the same implementation. Reflection dispatch allocates a small argument array per non-generic validation; typed parameter paths are unchanged.

The wrapper builds the original source for netstandard2.1 using the same support package versions already shipped in FishMMO Unity. Design-time tools are not added. FishMMO-Dependencies builds this project and copies its DLL over the normal NuGet Npgsql DLL only in Unity's Assets/Dependencies directory. Other .NET applications keep their existing NuGet driver. Rebuilding dependencies therefore cannot silently replace the fix with the unmodified package DLL.

To rebuild only the compatibility DLL:

dotnet build ThirdParty/Npgsql.UnityAot/Npgsql.UnityAot.csproj
dotnet msbuild FishMMO-Dependencies.csproj -t:CopyUnityAotNpgsql

After updating the DLL, rebuild the dedicated game server for the backend selected in the dashboard. Existing native IL2CPP players cannot consume a replacement managed DLL without rebuilding. Keep the server linker preservation rules as well: constructor stripping and runtime expression support were independent failures.

The native IL2CPP test also exposed a separate synchronous socket compatibility issue: Unity returned SocketError.InProgress (10036) for a non-blocking TCP connect, while Npgsql accepted only WouldBlock and aborted before its existing Select/error check. Both are valid pending-connect results on this path. The adapter now accepts both and leaves the existing timeout, readiness, error and socket cleanup logic intact.

Verified with Unity 6000.4.10f1: the unmodified driver reproduced the failure under Unity's AOT profile; the compatibility driver passed both framework-profile probes and actual standalone dedicated-server Mono and IL2CPP players. Checks include all 77 EF entity models, registry reads, asynchronous EF queries, tracked synthetic-row materialization, ten parameter roundtrips and validator exception propagation. No application rows were modified. The result files were not kept; FishMMO-Dependencies/Tools/DatabaseRuntimeProbe reruns the checks.
